title: Nouvelle AI
summary:
Nouvelle AI is an approach to artificial intelligence pioneered at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology AI Laboratory by the Australian American scientist Rodney Brooks during the latter half of the 1980s. A central idea of nouvelle AI is that simple behaviors combine to form more complex behaviors over time. For example, simple behaviors like "move forward" and "avoid obstacles" in a robot could combine to produce more complex behavior like chasing a moving object.

A nouvelle system refers continuously to its sensors rather than to an internal model of the world, processing external world information from the senses when it is required. The goal of traditional AI was to build intelligences without bodies that would only interact with the world via keyboard, screen, or printer. Nouvelle AI instead attempts to build embodied intelligence situated in the real world. It distances itself from strong AI, with its emphasis on human-level performance, in favour of the relatively modest aim of insect-level performance.

Nouvelle AI seeks to sidestep the frame problem by dispensing with filling the AI or robot with volumes of symbolic language and instead letting more complex behaviors emerge by combining simpler behavioral elements. Notable robots built using this approach include one that searched for empty soda cans in the busy offices of the MIT AI lab through 15 simple behavior units combining, as well as Genghis (a six-legged robot able to walk over rough terrain and follow humans) and Squirt (which would stay in dark corners until hearing a noise, then follow its source).

The conceptual shift introduced by nouvelle AI flourished in the robotics area, giving way to behavior-based robotics (BBR), a methodology for developing AI based on a modular decomposition of intelligence. Brooks' subsumption architecture was one of the earliest attempts to describe a mechanism for developing behavior-based AI. Brooks agreed that the level of nouvelle AI had come near the complexity of a real insect, raising questions about whether insect-level behavior was a reasonable goal.
